decisions.summary: The ledger and each ordinary short-path answer involve real model calls; this is not a model-skipping finding.
The deciding conversation receives the selected saved notes and request, and no applicable trusted instruction removal with material consequence is established.
No host correctness-based comparison or selection of two parseable short-path replies is shown; the violation concerns authority asserted in the deciding prompt.
A previous model's derived ledger is presented to the deciding model as already resolving every entry, with a directive to take its NOW or DATED value; it is not advisory.
The ledger reads the user's records using general change-history guidance; the inspected code does not prove an evaluation-derived input or output recipe.
The bounded review does not inspect endpoint dispatch and execution-ledger construction sufficiently to independently establish fidelity.
Held-record routing can divert a live-information request, but this record lacks a concrete offered applicable tool schema and valid blocked model-selected call.
The inspected short-path trigger is record and request based, not keyed on an evaluation identity.
